content: The inventory provides detailed information and hyperlinks to corresponding curriculum summaries, which are elaborated upon later in the guide. An Excel database containing this information is also available for download. The curricula included in this inventory were compiled and reported by their respective owners. If your curriculum is not listed, you can submit it for future inclusion by completing a designated form. The Elementary Traffic Safety Education Guide (ETSEG) is available for online purchase and is ideally used alongside a train-the-trainer course. Interested parties can receive training in Florida, which includes a companion teacher's guide. This guide offers a comprehensive, research-based, and classroom-tested safety curriculum. The ETSEG includes lessons on pedestrian, school bus, and bicycle safety, designed for 30and 45-minute increments, respectively. These lessons are supplemented with videos (in DVD format), detailed activity sheets, and optional video suggestions with ordering information. Additional components of the ETSEG include sections for student activities, enrichment activities, and guidance on adapting the modules for students with special needs. This guide provides a step-by-step approach to implementing an effective and cost-efficient pedestrian and bicycle safety education program. The Florida Traffic and Bicycle Safety Education Program has been successfully implemented in schools across Florida. It has served as a foundation for developing bicycle and pedestrian curricula nationwide. However, challenges include the need for a fleet of bicycles, classroom access, and dedicated funding to ensure ongoing teacher training. The Chicago Public School system adopted a pedestrian and school bus safety kit for approximately 250 Head Start programs. Child Safety Solutions is collaborating with the administration to monitor the program's implementation and effectiveness in meeting mandated safety requirements. Challenges include providing teachers with a low-cost, comprehensive teaching package that is developmentally appropriate and requires minimal additional training. Another challenge is offering a flexible teaching approach to meet Head Start certification requirements. The program features a large plastic roadway for practicing street crossing under various circumstances, with an emphasis on crossing with an adult for first-grade students. The PATH Ped Ed program has reached over 3,000 students since its relaunch in March 2009, with more than 22 instructors trained in its implementation. All participating teachers have requested the program's return, as indicated by satisfaction surveys. However, the program requires a trained instructor and specialized equipment to deliver consistent and accurate messaging. The primary challenge is securing funding for the program. Typically, up to six classes are scheduled per day over three to five days to reach all grades. The curriculum includes lessons on road rules, safe cycling skills, and improving walking and bicycling within school vicinities. It also features master pages in English and Spanish. The Cycling Across the Curriculum section allows teachers of math, science, English, and arts to integrate bicycle education into their activities. The program is free and has been available as part of a certification process since 1998. Over 3,700 Texas teachers and youth community workers have been trained, and trained college faculty have presented the material to more than 3,000 physical education students. Surveys estimate that over 200,000 Texas students annually receive bicycle safety lessons through the Safe Cyclist program. The program introduces students to inspiring individuals who overcome personal challenges and provides experiences in their respective sports. Physical activities emphasize walking, bicycling, and other forms of active transportation, helping students exceed national physical activity standards. Literacy development is also a focus, with students engaging in text-to-life connections and team-building activities. The Walk Across Illinois Afterschool Challenge is designed for schools, recreation centers, and other afterschool settings. The curriculum, created by classroom and physical education experts, is easy to understand and implement. In its first semester in 2010, the program engaged 660 children in Chicago. Teachers have praised the age-appropriate, resourceful, and engaging lesson plans, which have sparked meaningful discussions about walking and the environment. However, challenges include fitting the program into limited afterschool schedules, as some providers only have one to two hours with children, making it difficult to implement an 80-hour program. The curriculum includes simulated street crossing and bicycling practice, as well as in-class role-playing for bicycle and pedestrian safety. It is designed for grades 3-4 but can be adapted for other grades. The scripted curriculum guides teachers or afterschool providers through lessons, which can range from 1 to 80 hours. It includes 40 literacy-based and 40 physical activity-based lessons, which can be used throughout the school year or as standalone units. The program requires equipment typically found in classrooms or physical education settings, with a master list of materials provided. Lessons encourage students to think about reducing traffic and air pollution through walking, bicycling, and public transportation. They also highlight walking as a fun and healthy form of daily exercise. The curriculum includes both classroom and field activities, such as mapping routes from students' homes to schools, creating air pollution testers, and measuring breathing and heart rates before and after physical activity. Lessons have been reviewed by Massachusetts teachers and tested in classrooms with outstanding results. Teachers have reported that the lesson plans are age-appropriate, resourceful, and easy to implement, with students enjoying the activities and engaging in discussions about walking and the environment. The lesson plans are ready-to-use and do not require special equipment or outside assistance.
